generation.label: hook
generation.narration: That sudden loud roar when you start your car? It might not be your muffler.
generation.prompt: Close-up on the underside of a parked car at night, catalytic converter visibly bolted into the exhaust pipe, a security floodlight sweeping slowly across the metal casing; shallow depth of field, quiet empty parking lot in the background.
generation.negativePrompt: human face, person, hands, gloves, arms, talking head, low-res, blurry, extra fingers, plastic glow, oversaturated AI look, warped engine parts
generation.openingFrame: the converter sharply lit and centered, strongest possible first frame, unbranded, wordless

generation.label: symptom
generation.narration: A jarring, deep rumble the second the engine turns over — especially if it wasn't there the night before.
generation.prompt: Static low-angle shot of a car's exhaust tailpipe at engine start-up, dawn parking-lot light, a visible heat-shimmer and vapor pulsing from the pipe in time with the idle.
generation.negativePrompt: human face, person, hands, gloves, arms, talking head, low-res, blurry, extra fingers, plastic glow, oversaturated AI look, warped engine parts
generation.openingFrame: tailpipe centered, vapor pulse establishes immediately

generation.label: explanation
generation.narration: Catalytic converters hold small amounts of precious metal, which makes them a common target for thieves working fast, underneath the car.
generation.prompt: Object-only technical cutaway of a catalytic converter's internal honeycomb ceramic substrate, a faint metallic sheen along the coated surface, slow orbiting macro camera move; clean diagrammatic lighting, no text or labels rendered in-scene.
generation.negativePrompt: human face, person, hands, gloves, arms, talking head, low-res, blurry, extra fingers, plastic glow, oversaturated AI look, warped engine parts, on-screen text, logos, watermarks
generation.openingFrame: honeycomb substrate clearly readable at a glance

generation.label: consequence
generation.narration: It's become one of the most common theft claims nationwide — and a stolen converter usually means a full exhaust repair, not a quick patch.
generation.prompt: Overhead shot of a car raised on a shop lift, the exhaust pipe hanging with an empty gap where a converter used to be, a shop inspection light on a stand sweeping across the cut pipe ends; no hands present.
generation.negativePrompt: human face, person, hands, gloves, arms, talking head, low-res, blurry, extra fingers, plastic glow, oversaturated AI look, warped engine parts
generation.openingFrame: the gap in the exhaust pipe clearly readable, light sweep begins

generation.label: safe_action
generation.narration: One clue: an etched VIN or a welded shield can make your vehicle a harder target, and may help police trace it if it's ever stolen.
generation.prompt: Macro close-up on a catalytic converter shell showing a freshly etched VIN number and a welded anti-theft shield cage around it, an inspection light sweeping across the etched digits to make them legible, slow rack-focus.
generation.negativePrompt: human face, person, hands, gloves, arms, talking head, low-res, blurry, extra fingers, plastic glow, oversaturated AI look, warped engine parts
generation.openingFrame: etched digits and shield cage clearly readable, light beam entering frame

generation.label: branded_cta
generation.narration: Stop by and we'll take a look — Nick's Tire and Auto, on Euclid Avenue.
generation.prompt: Exterior establishing shot of Nick's Tire & Auto's shop bay, tire stack in foreground, late-afternoon light, logo signage visible and legible; camera holds steady for a clean end-card composite.
generation.negativePrompt: human face, person, hands, gloves, arms, talking head, low-res, blurry, extra fingers, plastic glow, oversaturated AI look, warped engine parts
generation.openingFrame: shop bay clearly readable, settles for a seamless hold into the freeze
